thread:
sam_support: FYI escalating BrightBeam dedicated pool 42 (eu-west-2-reserved-42). Customers seeing intermittent 429s and p95 token latency jumps after an autoscale event yesterday. suspect noisy neighbor / MIG interference. ticket #BB-8423 created.

maria_sre: Can you paste the short timeline + any API error snippets? need to know if 429 is rate limit or infra throttle.

sam_support: Timeline:
- 2024-11-05T02:12:03Z autoscale up +2 slices triggered (policy: burst)
- 02:13:20Z spike in p95 generation latency from ~120ms -> 1.4s
- 02:14:05Z repeat of 429s for a subset of BrightBeam keys (~30% of requests)
- 02:16:40Z autoscale completed, some requests still 429 until 02:28

Logs: (snip)
```
[02:13:20] /api/v1/generate 429 throttled run_queue
[02:13:21] runtime: KVCache miss contended, worker wait 18ms
[02:13:21] gpu0: MIG slice 2 busy 98% sm, sm_spike
[02:13:22] rate_limit: client_ok
```

sam_support: note rate_limit shows client_ok so it's infra-side.

jun_eng: pinging in. any node-level metrics? MIG packing / fragmenting?

arun_sre: pulled cluster telemetry - attached a short extract: several nodes in pool show transient SM utilization spikes and memory bandwidth noise concurrent with autoscale. one host (host-az3-17) had three MIG slices with mismatched profiles pinned to different tenants after the scale event.

jun_eng: interesting — can you share the MIG profiles and placement for host-az3-17? Also, did we fall back to software scheduling or rebind slices?

arun_sre: snapshot:
```
host-az3-17: nvidia-smi topo
MIG profiles: [1g.5gb@slice0: tenant=X], [4g.20gb@slice1: tenant=Y], [1g.5gb@slice2: tenant=BrightBeam]
NVLINK: normal
Kernel: 6.1.0
GPU temp: 78C
```

arun_sre: During autoscale we briefly repartitioned to fulfill burst requests; there are logs showing a synchronous partition change around 02:12:55 which aligns with the latency spike.

maria_sre: Repartitioning live can cause KV cache invalidations and small scheduling stalls — if BrightBeam had the KV cache warmed on slice2 it would take time to repopulate. but the 429s suggest request rejection due to worker throttling too. maybe we hit SM saturation and then runtime started returning 429s to protect SLOs.

jun_eng: Can we reproduce? steps to try on staging:
1) Pick a MIG-packed host in staging with mixed profiles
2) Load up tenant A to steady p95 ~100ms (serving loops, batch size 1)
3) Trigger autoscale to add a slice that forces repartition on that host
4) Run a BrightBeam-like workload concurrently (many short chat messages) and monitor sm_util, mem_bw, kvcache hitrate, and run_queue length

sam_support: I ran a quick smoke in staging and saw this: after repartition, kvcache hitrate dropped to 12% for 14s, run_queue doubled, and some requests returned 429 for 10s.

jun_eng: thanks. that confirms repro. hypothesis: dynamic MIG repartitioning on active hosts causes short-lived contention — two mechanisms: 1) kernel-level context stalls + memcpy pressure during profile resize, 2) runtime backpressure leading to request rejection for fairness. Both cause 429s timed with p95 spikes.

maria_sre: mitigation options:
- avoid live repartitioning on production reserved pools (require drain/resize window)
- when autoscale triggers, prefer scheduling new slices to underutilized hosts rather than repartitioning active hosts (policy change)
- increase KVCache timeout/replication for critical tenants to reduce warmup pain

jun_eng: short-term hotfix: implement a quick guard preventing repartition on a host with >70% sm_util or with >1 active tenant with hot KVCache. I'll open a PR to the autoscaler policies.

sam_support: customer note: BrightBeam saw billing anomalies where their token-count dropped during the 02:13-02:18 window and then bounced. are we sure billing didn't double charge?

arun_sre: billing pipeline logs show a small gap in event ingestion corresponding to the throttled requests; we did not double-charge, but some requests were marked failed and refunded per policy. ops-bot recorded refund tx #RF-9932.

ticket-bot: Ticket BB-8423 updated: root cause: transient MAG/partition noise during live repartition; mitigation planned (autoscaler policy change). ETA: PR review by tomorrow.

maria_sre: Action items:
- jun: PR to prevent live repartitioning on hot hosts (priority P0)
- arun: sweep of reserved pools for other hosts with live repartition events in last 7 days
- sam: communicate RCA and refund summary to BrightBeam (cc: account exec)

jun_eng: putting up draft PR: autoscaler now prefers 'new-host-first' placement and refuses in-place repartition if sm_util>0.7 or kvcache_hitrate>0.2. will add logs to surface partition attempts.

sam_support: thanks team — I'll update BrightBeam and keep this thread linked to BB-8423. :thumbsup:

maria_sre: one followup — let's also add a small repro harness in infra-tests that runs repartition during load to catch regressions. low-effort test but high signal.

jun_eng: agreed, adding test to infra-regressions.

ops-bot: deploy-batch: autoscaler-policy-v2 scheduled to deploy to staging at 2024-11-06T03:00:00Z

sam_support: closing loop here, will reopen if customer sees further 429s.
